title: Customer escalation war-room notes - INC-4321
summary: Prep and running notes for P1 customer escalation (INC-4321). Customer reports timeouts and degraded throughput for their dedicated pool after rolling a new model version. Initial hypothesis: kernel selection/quantization mismatch on a subset of nodes causing slow token generation and CPU fallback. Goal: stabilize customer workload within 2 hours, patch and post-mortem next day.
context: Customer: NovaDocs (legal-docs SaaS). Dedicated pool on us-west-2, 8xA100s, pinned to model redwood-legal-v2-quant. Rollout triggered yesterday (2026-03-01 18:12 UTC). Error spike and latency increase observed starting 2026-03-02 02:45 UTC. Customer escalated at 2026-03-02 03:20 UTC. Incident created JIRA-INC-4321.
agenda:
1) Quick sync on current state (5m)
2) Confirm impact and customer ask (5m)
3) Ownership and immediate mitigation (10m)
4) Short-term rollback/patch plan (10m)
5) Communication plan with customer (5m)
6) Action items and owners (5m)
timeline:
- 2026-03-02 02:45 UTC: first latency spike in telemetry (console)
- 2026-03-02 03:05 UTC: automated alert routed to eng-sre
- 2026-03-02 03:20 UTC: customer opened support escalation call
- 2026-03-02 03:45 UTC: initial triage complete (identified increased CPU fallback on 2 nodes)
- 2026-03-02 04:10 UTC: war-room convened (this doc created)
- ongoing: collecting logs and kernel traces
impact:
- Customer throughput down ~60% for critical inference route (document-extract)
- Average p95 latency increased from 140ms -> 2.1s for affected requests
- No data exfiltration; requests still completing but poorly degraded
- Business impact: NovaDocs legal-review customers experiencing timeouts, risk of SLA breach
hypothesis:
- Recent model build used a different quantization packing that triggers slow fallback kernels on some nodes
- Kernel selection heuristics mis-detect hardware capabilities on 2/8 nodes after minor driver update (2026-02-28)
- KV cache pressure combined with new model memory layout -> CPU spillover
investigations_in_progress:
- SRE: gather dmesg + driver logs from affected nodes (Samir)
- Infra: check recent OS/driver package diffs for nodes in pool (Riley)
- Serving-runtime: reproduce locally with redwood-legal-v2-quant + sample workload (Dana)
- Telemetry: correlate request ids from customer traces to failing nodes (Morgan)
immediate_mitigation_plan:
Option A (favored): Pin NovaDocs to previous model variant (redwood-legal-v1-quant) for dedicated pool; route traffic to healthy nodes.
Option B: temporary rollback of driver update on affected nodes and restart serving runtime.
Decision: Pin to v1 for immediate customer relief, then do controlled driver rollback if pinning insufficient.
